nodes.summary: For a finite matroid $M$ and every element $i$, the sum over all nonempty proper flats, since each flat either contains $i$ or does not.
nodes.title: The classes $\alpha_M$ and $\beta_M$ add up to the sum of all generators

i j} x_F$ in the Chow ring; this is a generator of the ideal $J_M$ when $i

nodes.title: The class $\alpha_M$ does not depend on the element

nodes.summary: For an element $i$ of the ground set, $\alpha_{M,i} = \sum_{F \ni i} x_F$, the sum over the nonempty proper flats containing $i$. By the linear relations its class $\alpha_M$ in $A^1(M)_\mathbb{R}$ does not depend on $i$. The class $\alpha_M$ is nef (AHK Lemma 9.7), and for a loopless matroid of rank $r + 1$ the class $\alpha_M^r$ has degree $1$ (AHK Proposition 5.10).
nodes.title: The class $\alpha_M$

nodes.summary: For a finite matroid $M$ and elements $i, j$ of its ground set, $\beta_{M,i} = \beta_{M,j}$ in the Chow ring: subtract $\alpha_{M,i} = \alpha_{M,j}$ from $\alpha_{M,i} + \beta_{M,i} = \sum_F x_F = \alpha_{M,j} + \beta_{M,j}$.
nodes.title: The class $\beta_M$ does not depend on the element

nodes.summary: For an element $i$ of the ground set, $\beta_{M,i} = \sum_{F \not\ni i} x_F$, the sum over the nonempty proper flats not containing $i$. Its class $\beta_M$ in $A^1(M)_\mathbb{R}$ does not depend on $i$, since $\alpha_{M,i} + \beta_{M,i}$ is the sum of all the $x_F$. The class $\beta_M$ is nef (AHK Lemma 9.7).
nodes.title: The class $\beta_M$

nodes.summary: In the polynomial ring $S_M = \mathbb{R}[x_F]$, with one variable for each nonempty proper flat $F$ of $M$, the ideal $I_M$ is generated by the monomials $x_{F_1} x_{F_2}$ for incomparable flats $F_1, F_2$, and the ideal $J_M$ by the linear forms for distinct elements $i_1, i_2$ of the ground set. This is the ideal $I_M + J_M$.
nodes.title: The Chow ideal $I_M + J_M$ of a matroid

nodes.summary: The Chow ring of a matroid $M$ is the polynomial ring with one variable for each nonempty proper flat, modulo the incomparability relations $x_{F_1} x_{F_2} = 0$ and the linear relations $\sum_{F \ni i_1} x_F = \sum_{F \ni i_2} x_F$.
nodes.title: The Chow ring $A^*(M)_\mathbb{R}$ of a matroid

nodes.summary: For every function $c$ on subsets of the ground set, the class $\ell(c) = \sum_F c_F \, x_F$ lies in $A^1(M)_\mathbb{R}$. This is where the hard Lefschetz theorem and the Hodge–Riemann relations use it: multiplication by $\ell(c)^{r-2q}$ maps $A^q(M)_\mathbb{R}$ into $A^{r-q}(M)_\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The Lefschetz class has degree one

nodes.summary: For a function $c$ on subsets of the ground set, $\ell(c)$ is the class of $\sum_F c_F \, x_F$ in $A^1(M)_\mathbb{R}$, the sum over all nonempty proper flats $F$. When $c$ is strictly submodular, $\ell(c)$ is the Lefschetz class of the hard Lefschetz theorem and the Hodge–Riemann relations.
nodes.title: The class $\ell(c)$

nodes.summary: For a finite loopless matroid $M$ of rank $r + 1$ there is exactly one linear map $\deg : A^*(M)_\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ that vanishes off degree $r$ and takes the value $1$ on $x_{F_1} \cdots x_{F_r}$ for every flag of nonempty proper flats $F_1 \subsetneq \cdots \subsetneq F_r$. It restricts to an isomorphism $A^r(M)_\mathbb{R} \cong \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The degree map of a matroid

nodes.summary: $A^q(M)_\mathbb{R}$ is the image in the Chow ring of the homogeneous polynomials of degree $q$ in the variables $x_F$. Since $I_M + J_M$ is generated by homogeneous elements, these subspaces form a grading of $A^*(M)_\mathbb{R}$. For a loopless matroid of rank $r + 1$, $A^r(M)_\mathbb{R} \cong \mathbb{R}$ through the degree map.
nodes.title: Graded piece $A^q(M)_\mathbb{R}$ of the Chow ring

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a finite loopless matroid of rank $r + 1$ and let $\ell = \ell(c)$ be the class of a strictly submodular function $c$. For every integer $q$ with $2q \le r$, multiplication by $\ell^{r-2q}$ is a bijection In Lean: every $b \in A^{r-q}(M)_\mathbb{R}$ equals $\ell^{r-2q} a$ for exactly one $a \in A^q(M)_\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Hard Lefschetz theorem for matroids

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a finite loopless matroid of rank $r + 1$, $\deg$ its degree map, and $\ell = \ell(c)$ the class of a strictly submodular function $c$. For every integer $q$ with $2q \le r$, the symmetric bilinear form on $A^q(M)_\mathbb{R}$ is positive definite on the kernel of multiplication by $\ell^{r-2q+1}$: if $a \in A^q(M)_\mathbb{R}$ is nonzero and $\ell^{r-2q+1} a = 0$, then $(-1)^q \deg(a \, \ell^{r-2q} a) > 0$.
nodes.title: Hodge–Riemann relations for matroids

nodes.summary: A linear map $\deg : A^*(M)_\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a degree map for $r$ if it vanishes on every graded piece $A^q(M)_\mathbb{R}$ with $q \ne r$ and satisfies for every flag $F_1 \subsetneq F_2 \subsetneq \cdots \subsetneq F_r$ of nonempty proper flats. For a loopless matroid of rank $r + 1$ these flags are the maximal ones, and the monomials $x_{F_1} \cdots x_{F_r}$ correspond to the $r$-dimensional cones of…
nodes.title: Degree map of a matroid of rank $r + 1$

nodes.summary: For a finite matroid on $E$, the function $I \mapsto |I| \, |E \setminus I|$ is strictly submodular. In particular strictly submodular functions exist, so the hypotheses of the hard Lefschetz theorem and the Hodge–Riemann relations can be met.
nodes.title: A strictly submodular function

nodes.summary: A real function $c$ on the nonempty proper subsets of the ground set $E$ is strictly submodular if for any two incomparable subsets $I_1, I_2 \subseteq E$, where $c(\emptyset)$ and $c(E)$ are replaced by zero. In Lean $c$ is a function on all sets with $c(\emptyset) = c(E) = 0$; its values on sets not contained in $E$ play no role.
nodes.title: Strictly submodular function

nodes.summary: For a matroid $M$ on $E$, the nonempty proper flats are the flats $F$ of $M$ (Mathlib's `Matroid.IsFlat`) with $F \ne \emptyset$ and $F \ne E$. They index the variables $x_F$ of the Chow ring. For a loopless matroid $\emptyset$ is a flat, and these are the flats strictly between the bottom and the top of the lattice of flats.
nodes.title: Nonempty proper flats of a matroid

nodes.summary: For a finite loopless matroid $M$ of rank $r + 1$, its degree map $\deg$, any element $i$ of the ground set and every $k \le r$, where $\mu_k(M)$ is the unsigned coefficient of $\lambda^{r-k}$ in $\chi_M(\lambda)/(\lambda - 1)$.
nodes.title: Reduced characteristic polynomial coefficients as mixed degrees

nodes.summary: Each generator $x_F$ of the Chow ring lies in $A^1(M)_\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Generators have degree one

nodes.summary: If $F$ and $G$ are nonempty proper flats with $F \not\subseteq G$ and $G \not\subseteq F$, then $x_F \, x_G = 0$ in the Chow ring. Consequently a nonzero monomial in the $x_F$ is supported on a chain of flats.
nodes.title: Incomparable flats multiply to zero

nodes.summary: For a nonempty proper flat $F$ of $M$, $x_F$ is the class of the variable $x_F$ in the Chow ring $A^*(M)_\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: The generator $x_F$ of the Chow ring
Combinatorics

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
